title: Identifying Neuro-cognitive-physiological Factors that Moderate Anxiety and Depression
summary:
Anxiety and depression disorders are common and often co-occur, with moderate treatment success. Current diagnosis methods rely on self-reported symptoms, which can be inaccurate. New research suggests combining brain, body, and mind data could improve diagnosis.
Our project aims to change how we diagnose anxiety and depression by looking at cognitive biases, physiological reactions, and brain activity. We will use fMRI, heart rate variability, blood pressure, and cognitive tasks to investigate whether these combined factors can better diagnose these conditions and find different subtypes.
We have previously predicted anxiety and depression diagnoses and symptoms using machine learning models and cognitive tasks. Brain imaging studies have shown specific patterns and reactions in people with these conditions. By combining these methods, we hope to find markers that can improve diagnostic tools and treatments.
150 individuals with anxiety and depression diagnoses and 150 healthy individuals will participate in the study and complete cognitive tasks for fMRI, focusing on attention, expectancy, and interpretation biases. Our analysis will include Machine learning models to distinguish between the clinical group and controls and identify subtypes within the clinical group. Our goal is to integrate into the psychiatric diagnosis a more precise, personalized approach based on cognitive, neural, and physiological markers.

interventions.name: Individuals diagnosed with anxiety and/or depression disorders, undergoing task-based and resting-state fMRI, ECG, and blood pressure measurements, combined with cognitive tasks.
Healthy control participants undergoing the same measurements as the clinical group.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Only for the anxiety and depression group: Psychiatric diagnosis of anxiety disorder (including panic attacks, agoraphobia, generalized anxiety, social anxiety, adjustment disorder with anxious reaction and anxiety-NOS) and/or mood disorder (major depression, dysphoria, adjustment disorder with depressive reaction, depressive episode). 
- Age 18-55
- Normal or corrected-to-normal vision
- Voluntary participation and signing of the declaration of consent
- German as a mother tongue or fluency in German (CEFR C1)
Exclusion criteria:
- Active psychosis
- Diagnosis of bipolar disorder/ history of manic episodes
- Significant suicidal intent requiring enhanced care
- Presence of any contraindications for MRI examinations (see Appendix 1E MRI consent form) including claustrophobia, pacemakers, intracranial metal clips, cochlear implants, cerebrospinal fluid shunts, braces, and implanted medication pumps. 
- Neurological illnesses (e.g., epilepsy) or head trauma
- Persons unable to give consent (e.g., in the case of dementia)
- Pregnancy or planned pregnancy at the time of the study
- Breastfeeding women
- Lack of consent to the disclosure of incidental findings
- Only for the control group: Diagnosis of anxiety and/or mood disorders 
- Only for the control group: Previous or current psychiatric diagnosis (not including ADHD)
